[Rating: 1/10] A few plays on BGA. Multiplayer solo. You just put cards on a 5x5 grid. You cannot see the other players boards/grids (not that it will count that much, because if you could, it will be instant AP, since it will be a lot of info to process).  There is a winning strategy. If you can find it, you will win for shure in most cases.  For a game published in 2026 it has too many designing mistakes, hence the low rating. I don't like to rate games with 1 star, but in some cases I don't have any other option.

[Rating: 1/10] Game concept seems fundamentally flawed for scoring each row and column poker hand against the corresponding ones of your opponents, when these are all hidden behind screens until the end of the game. A well-arranged grid will beat a poorly-arranged one, but two broadly equal grids will just resolve according to where players happened to arbitrarily place their best hands.

[Rating: 3/10] I really don't like these type of hidden bingo style game.  I'm ok with multiplayer solitaire bingo-style (love Super Mega Lucky Box, enjoy Lucky Numbers), but you get to spectate how others are doing and it's up to how effective each player does (e.g. there's a similar game where you simply score based on how good a poker hand you did in each row/column). This winner-takes-all formula where you get nothing for having the 2nd best hand in a row, but have no clue how others are doing, just makes it feel random on top of random.

[Rating: 5/10] A bingo like game with poker influences where players are to announce 25 card (from normal deck) and one at a time place a tile in an empty space on a 5x5 grid. Cards may have events (may restrict players from placing from specific positions). All rows/columns/diagonals are scored via poker hands. The player with the most points wins.

[Rating: 5/10] I don't necessarily dislike it, but I won't remember it past tomorrow. There are many other games I'd rather play with a 52 card deck. The winner-take-all per row without having at least a hint of where cards are being placed drop it from a 6 to a 5.

[Rating: 5/10] 8/21/26:5-lives up to its name. Flip 25 cards one at a time to place them into a 5x5 grid. Then compare all 5 rows, 5 columns, and 2 diagonals against your opponents who did the same. A fine lark, but nothing super interesting.

[Rating: 5/10] Cute and fun. Easy and quick filler, would play again at anytime, but it's still just a filler.

[Rating: 5/10] It's ok not very little control over your score. Just hope for the best trying to make as many poker hands across rows and columns as you can. Some of the scoring cards are objectively better/easier.
